ABORIGINAL AFFAIRS  The Government's policies for Aboriginal Australians aim to:  - encourage Aboriginal self-management and support Aboriginal initiative and enterprise.  - provide Aboriginal with equal access to all services provided by all levels of Government.  - provide additional assistance to reduce the special disadvantages from which Aboriginal in many cases still suffer.  PAST ACHIEVEMENTS.  In support of those objectives the Government established the Aboriginal Development Commission which provides funding for Aboriginal housing and supports Aboriginal enterprises and the purchase and development of land.  The National Aboriginal Conference has been established, a fully elected body of  Aboriginal from throughout Australia whose National Executive acts as an advisor to the Government on all aspects of Aboriginal Affairs.  The Government has supported specialist Aboriginal medical and legal services which provide essential services to Aboriginal, especially those remote from or unable to use existing general community services.  It has, also provided substantial funds to Aboriginal Hostels Ltd., a company which provides a range of accommodation for Aboriginal requiring temporary accommodation.  The Government has also given special attention to increasing Aboriginal employment opportunities and has sought to improve Aboriginal education and training.  In its next term of office the Government will seek to build on those policies, continuing to support programs which will reduce Aboriginal disadvantage in areas such as health, housing, education, employment and legal aid.  NEW POLICIES.  1. FRINGE DWELLERS/EXCISIONS.  The Government recognizes the special needs of Aboriginal fringe dwellers or town campers identified by the House of Representatives Standing Committee on Aboriginal Affairs in its report "Strategies to Help Overcome the Problems of Aboriginal Town Camps". It therefore has decided to extend the responsibilities of Aboriginal Hostels Limited to allow it to plan for the shelter and housing of town campers.  The Government will also develop a program to assist those Aboriginal currently living on pastoral properties in the Northern Territory who will be eligible for excisions under proposals agreed to by the Commonwealth and Territory Governments.  2. ABORIGINAL SPORTS ASSISTANCE.  In recognition of the need to provide opportunities for Aboriginal fulfillment and achievement in other fields the government is expanding the level of support for Aboriginal sports assistance throughout Australia.  A series of initiatives developed from advice from the National Aboriginal Conference will be implemented to encourage Aboriginal sportsmen and women to achieve excellence, to increase community participation in sports, and to develop and upgrade sporting facilities which can be used by Aboriginal communities.  3. ABORIGINAL CULTURAL HERITAGE.  Aboriginal people attach great importance to their art and cultural traditions. The Government is increasing its efforts in assisting Aboriginal to preserve their cultural heritage in consultation with the National Aboriginal Conference and other relevant organizations in this field. The Government will seek to develop initiatives in several areas, including:  - the identification, preservation and display of Aboriginal art, artifacts and significant natural sites.  - the dissemination of information on Aboriginal culture and tradition.  - the performance of Aboriginal traditional art.  - increased employment opportunities in areas where Aboriginal can be responsible for preserving and explaining their own culture and heritage.  4. ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT.  In recognition of the increasing importance of the local government role in meeting the needs of their Aboriginal citizens the Government will therefore provide direct grants to local government to assist in projects and programs on a cooperative basis.  5. TASK FORCES FOR TRAINING ABORIGINAL.  There are today over 900 independent Aboriginal organizations providing community and other assistance to Aboriginal throughout Australia.  In order to assist the work of these independent bodies, the Government has decided to fund the creation of a number of Task Forces which will combine the skills of relevant institutions to provide training for financial, administrative, health and field officers from medical and legal organizations working in a diverse range of Aboriginal communities.  Wherever possible, the Task Forces will use the skills of Aboriginal people with the necessary qualifications and experience.  YOUNG PEOPLE  The Government has upgraded the Office of Youth Affairs, to ensure that the process of government is more accessible and responsive to the aspirations of young Australians. We are anxious that the views of young people are fully taken account of in the development of Government policies and programs.  The Government is committed to seeing that International Youth Year 1985 is not  simply a symbolic commemoration of Australian youth and that the year is used to examine questions underlying the role and potential of young people and the issues which concern them.  A Commonwealth grant of $100 000 is enabling the Youth Affairs Council of Australia to consult the entire range of Government and voluntary youth organizations on youth-related issues. It is expected that this process will be completed by April and recommendations put to a meeting of Federal and State Youth Affairs Ministers in time for pre-budget discussions.  The Government has demonstrated its concern for the adverse effects that a difficult labor market has on youth. Our programs relating to school-to-work transition, work experience and apprenticeship have all been upgraded.  Funding for Youth Affairs Programs (including CYSS) have been increased by 25 per cent in 1982/83. $100 million has been earmarked in the Wage Pause program for employment projects to assist youth.  We are committed to helping homeless youth. $7.6 million of the $10 million 3 year program to help homeless youth has already been committed to 65 projects. In addition in 1982/83 we allocated $300 000 for a pilot project to assist non-government organizations in providing for young homeless people receiving unemployment benefits.  WOMEN  The Government's policy is to ensure that Australian women have equal opportunity, equality of status in society, and freedom from discrimination in every way.  It has established the National Women's Advisory Council, which provides wide-ranging advice to the Government on matters affecting women. The Council consists of twelve members appointed from all parts of Australia and is widely representative of Australian women.  In addition, the Office of the Status of Women co-ordinates Government policies relating to women.  The Government has announced its intention to introduce legislation during the next Parliamentary Session to prohibit discrimination on grounds of sex in Commonwealth employment while in the Australian Capital Territory the prohibitions will extend to education, housing and access to goods and services.  It has established as a target in job creation programs funded by the Commonwealth that 50 per cent of the jobs created should go to women and girls.  THE ARTS  The Government's objective is to promote excellence in the creative and performing arts.  It has continued to support the Australia Council, the International Cultural Corporation and Artbank, and through their wide ranging activities an increasing number of Australians has been able to participate in and enjoy the Arts.  The Government has increased its funding of NIDA - the National Institute of Dramatic Art, and is building a new home for NIDA on the campus of the University of New South Wales.  It has completed the Australian National Gallery which was opened by HM the Queen in October 1982, and is providing $27 million over the next five years for the acquisition of great works of art by the time of the Bicentenary in 1988.  The Tax Incentives Scheme, whereby the value of gifts of works of art and other cultural property given to public institutions is deductible from income tax has been made permanent.  The Australian film industry receives strong support from the Government. It has continued to fund the Australian Film Commission and Film Australia, and has introduced a tax incentives scheme which has been instrumental in ensuring that private investment in Australian films is maintained at a high level. The Government recently agreed to modify the scheme to make it even more attractive to Australian investors; by providing that a film for which a tax deduction was claimed might be made during a two year period, rather than in 12 months as has previously been the case.  The Government is also proceeding with the construction of a new building for the Australian Film and Television School near Macquarie University in Sydney.  The Government will establish a national touring and access fund by advancing $1 million to the Australia Council for the purposes of showing the best artistic achievements to Australians in all States. The main flagship companies and works of art will be shown in all States and assistance will be provided to State-based theatre, music and other groups to tour in country areas. City based groups will receive assistance to perform in outer suburbs.  HERITAGE.  The Government's aim is to ensure that Australia's cultural and natural heritage is identified and safeguarded. It recognizes that this is a responsibility which it shares with the States; its policy is to work closely with the States and to provide national leadership where appropriate.  It has continued to support the Australian Heritage Commissioner, the National Estate Grants program and the National Trust. $12.75 million has been provided for these during the last three years.  It has actively supported the World Heritage Convention; five properties nominated by the Government are now on the World Heritage List - The Great Barrier Reef, Kakadu National Park, the Willandra Lakes, Lord Howe Island, and South-West Tasmania.  The Government will provide $50 million over five years to assist the Tasmanian Government to develop South-West Tasmania as a Wilderness Park of world class.  Substantial areas of the Great Barrier Reef have been declared as part of the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park which is now the largest Marine Park in the world.  The Government has decided to accelerate the work of the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority, in order that the rest of the Great Barrier Reef might be added to the Marine Park within three years. The Government is also concerned that Australia's cultural heritage is preserved and made available to the Australian people. It has established the Museum of Australia: building extensions and is significantly upgrading of the collections and displays at the Australian War Memorial; and commenced construction of a new National Archives headquarters building in Canberra. Major extensions to the National Library of Australia are also under way. The Government has also announced its support for a program of national and international activities to celebrate Australia's Bicentenary in 1988, and will provide an estimated $166 million for this purpose over the next five years. It has established the National Australia Day Committee, which has over the last few years significantly increased the interest of Australians in Australia Day, through a wide-ranging program of events conducted throughout the nation in co-operation with the State Australia Day Committees.  SPORT  Australians justifiably take pride in their sporting achievements, and the Government recognizes that it has a responsibility to assist Australian athletes to attain the highest standard of performance. The Government has sought to do this via:  - Introduction of a Sports Development Program which has assisted the national organization of 76 sports in the areas of administration, coaching and international competition.  - Development of the National Athlete Award Scheme under which world ranked athletes and teams receive assistance for training and competition.  - Establishment of the National Committee on Sport and Recreation for the Disabled and provision of funds to encourage disabled people to participate in sport and recreation.  - Financial support for the Commonwealth Games Association and the Australian Olympic Federation to help our teams prepare for and participate in these international events.  - Commitment of $25 million over three years on a dollar-for-dollar basis with the States to assist with the development of sporting facilities of international standard.  - Provision of funds to establish a national secretariat to co-ordinate the implementation of the first Australia Games in Sydney in 1984.  - Establishment of the Australian Institute of Sport in Canberra where 188 gifted Australian athletes are receiving high level coaching in one of the eight resident sports.  Consistent with its policy of encouraging private sector involvement in community activities, the Government has decided to replace the successful National Athlete Award Scheme with a Sports Aid Foundation which will be established outside of Government and run by a group of able people from the business community. The Foundation will receive Government support of $0.5 million in each of its first two years of operation and contributions to the Foundation by companies and private individuals will be tax deductible.  LAW REFORM  The Government is committed to continuing its already impressive list of achievements in law reform designed to help families and individuals.  INTEGRATED COURTS.  The Government believes that all Superior Courts in Australia should have jurisdiction under both Federal and States laws with a right of appeal to a new National Court of Appeal. The High Court will remain as the final court of appeal in all cases as well as constitutional cases.  The Government will support this proposal at the next Constitutional Convention and will negotiate with the States to obtain the necessary agreement to give effect to it.  SIMPLER AND LESS LEGISLATION.  The Government is disturbed at the volume and complexity of legislation which often places new and unnecessary burdens upon the people. The Attorney-General has already taken steps to obtain support for a new approach to drafting legislation and its application by the courts.  The Government will accelerate this process as far as it can and will limit the volume of its own legislation.  1. FAMILY LAW.  The Attorney-General will reintroduce a Bill to amend the Family Law Act.  One amendment will propose that a spouse who can afford to do so will be required to make more realistic payments to the other spouse entitled to support and particularly for the children.  The Government will also establish a Matrimonial Property Inquiry immediately following the election. The Inquiry will be asked to set out the ground rules for the allocation of property between husbands and wives in the event of a marriage breaking down. The Inquiry has the support of a Joint Committee of the Parliament and the Family Law Council.  2. CONSUMER EDUCATION.  The Commonwealth Government will continue to support consumer education activities in the community.  It will continue in its role as a catalyst and coordinator for consumer education activities with the States and Territories.  The Commonwealth Government has given support in principle to the establishment of a Consumer Education Foundation which would serve as a resource, research and referral center, promote greater co-operative efforts between business, government and consumer groups and advance consumer education in schools and community groups.  3. SEX DISCRIMINATION.  Legislation to prohibit discrimination on the ground of sex and marital status in any field of Commonwealth employment will be introduced. This discrimination will also be prohibited in the Australian Capital Territory in the areas of private employment, bank loans, housing loans, accommodation, insurance, partnerships and professional organizations.  The Government is proceeding with the process of ratifying the Covenant on the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women.  4. CRIMINAL INVESTIGATION BILL.  The Government will proceed in the new Parliament with the Criminal Investigation Bill. The legislation demonstrates the Government's desire to preserve and maintain civil liberties consistently with the requirements of law enforcement and stability in the community.  The Criminal Investigation Bill sets out the rights and duties of a police officer and the citizen with whom he deals in the course of investigating a Commonwealth criminal offence.  There have been many consultations and modifications to the Bill since the original Law Reform Commission Report and early in the new Parliament a new Bill taking into account the comments received will be introduced.  IMMIGRATION AND ETHNIC AFFAIRS  The Government will continue to recognize the importance of reuniting separated families, and to do its part as a responsible member of the international community to assist in the settling of refugees.  The size and composition of the immigration program will be kept under review to ensure that it continues to reflect Australia's capacity to settle migrants successfully (taking into consideration the prevailing economic circumstances).  Government programs have been directed towards giving migrants genuine equality of opportunity as full and equal members of the Australian community. To achieve this the Government has established, in partnership with ethnic groups, a range of migrant services and facilities unrivalled by any other country.  LEARNING ENGLISH.  The Government recognizes that inability to speak English is the most serious impediment to successful settlement. Over $100 million is now spent on special education programs each year. These include:  - The Adult Migrant Education Program which has been expanded fourfold over the past five years.  - A new program of advanced English courses at TAFE colleges to commence this year.  - The Child Migrant Education Program.  The Telephone Interpreter Service will be further enhanced to provide a service for all residents of Australia, wherever they may live, for the cost of a local call.  Increased emphasis will also be placed upon the recruitment of bilingual staff in the Public Service, especially into positions involving extensive public contact.  WELFARE AND SETTLEMENT SERVICES.  The Government will continue to expand its grants to ethnic community groups and voluntary agencies to fund the provision of welfare and other services such as:  - Grants-in Aid to community organizations to employ social welfare workers.  - The Migrant Project Subsidy Scheme to help ethnic groups develop facilities and services.  ETHNIC MEDIA.  Australian society has been enriched by the diversity of cultures presented through the multicultural television network, Channel 0/28.  - The Government is committed to expand this service throughout Australia during the next three years.  - It will take steps to enhance ethnic radio services after considering submissions from the public later this year.  AUSTRALIAN CITIZENSHIP.  The Government believes that Australian citizenship is the cornerstone of Australia's national identity.  - The Australian Citizenship Act will be amended to eliminate discriminatory elements and to enhance the status of citizenship.  - New procedures are being instituted to ensure applications are processed quickly.  RECIPROCAL AGREEMENTS ON SOCIAL SECURITY.  The Government has indicated its willingness to enter into negotiations with migrant source countries that have a common interest in establishing reciprocal social security agreements. Such negotiations would aim to establish where it was possible to conclude agreements of mutual benefit to Australia and these other countries. Reciprocal social security agreements are the usual method countries use to protect the pension rights of people moving from one country to another.  GRANT-IN-AID.  The Government has decided to provide a $50 000 grant-in-aid to the Federation of Ethnic Community Councils.  A STRONG AND SECURE AUSTRALIA  FOREIGN AFFAIRS  In recent years Australia's stature as a Middle Power has increased significantly the range of our international activities and the weight of our responsibilities.  The Government's policies have added strength to Australia's bonds with the Western Alliance - countries with which we share deeply rooted concepts of freedom and personal liberty.  Australia's alignment with the West, however, has not affected the strengthening of links with the developing countries of our own and other regions. Indeed, it has been a positive help in enabling us to act as a bridge between the developed and developing countries.  The Government recognizes that Australia's political and strategic environment is shaped by its location in the Asia/Pacific region. This region has developed great economic significance, including as it does the economic vitality of Japan, South Korea and ASEAN, the vast populations of China and India, and the huge areas of the Indian and Pacific Oceans with their island communities.  Vital trading links with major trading partners such as Japan are being sustained and further developed. It is also necessary to strengthen understanding with the developing countries in our region and increase their capacity for economic growth and stability; at the same time Australia must be part of a basic security system which will safeguard its interest in the face of Soviet pressures.  The Government has adopted a forward looking foreign policy, and today Australia's voice is listened to with respect in the Western Alliance, the Commonwealth, the Third World, in China and Japan, and in regional forums such as ASEAN and the South Pacific Forum and the United Nations.  Government Policy aims to:  - Ensure the security, independence and continued prosperity of Australia.  - Seek resolution of the problems preventing the achievement of lasting world peace.  - Support our allies, and at the same time, play a role in seeking moderation and conciliation in world affairs.  - Advance the social and political values upon which Australian society is founded, in particular individual freedom, opportunity and prosperity.  - Promote international initiatives designed to boost economic growth and improve economic relationships between the developed and developing world.  THE WESTERN ALLIANCE.  The ANZUS Treaty and Australia's ties with the wider Western Alliance remain central to our foreign policy and a vital link in the interlocking security arrangements safeguarding the free world.  The burden of maintaining peace and protecting democracy, however, is now beyond the capacity of any single country to shoulder alone. Accordingly, our policies provide for:  - The Five Power Defense arrangements with Malaysia, Singapore, New Zealand and the United Kingdom.  - Joint facilities in Australia.  - Joint exercises with Allies.  - Access to our ports by allied ships.  - The B-52 Agreement.  - Defense cooperation programs with ASEAN countries and the South Pacific.  All these activities are now important parts of the complex net of arrangements which make up the strategic strength of the free world.  The ANZUS Treaty is the anchor to the southern end of the West's line of defense in Asia and the Pacific.  Together with the other members of the Western Alliance the Australian Government has strongly opposed the Soviet Union's:  - Invasion and occupation of Afghanistan.  - Military support for Vietnam.  - Growing forces particularly naval, in the Asia Pacific Region.  - Initial probes in the South Pacific.  PEACEKEEPING AND DISARMAMENT.  Australia has a long and proud record of contributing to peacekeeping in world trouble spots such as Korea, Kashmir, Cyprus and the Middle East.  Australia also contributed to the Commonwealth cease-fire monitoring force in the Rhodesian (Zimbabwe) election and, if requested to do so, will contribute to a United Nations force arising out of an agreement on the Namibian problem.  The failure of United Nations machinery - due particularly to obstruction by the Soviet Union - has forced free world countries, including Australia, to go outside the United Nations for alternative peacekeeping arrangements. With the Sinai Multinational Peacekeeping Force the choice was stark - alternative peacekeeping operations or the risk of no peace at all.  Withdrawal of Australia's contingent would sabotage the single most important step in the process of achieving peace in the Middle East and be against the expressed wishes of the people of both Israel and Egypt.  Australia has given consistent support to responsible disarmament measures. Australia is an active member of the International Committee on Disarmament (CD), and was an active participant in the 1982 United Nations Special Session on Disarmament.  Australia believes that to be effective, any disarmament agreement must contain proper verification and compliance measures.  To validate the Australian Government's uranium export policy stringent and comprehensive nuclear safeguards agreements for the export of Australian uranium have now been negotiated with the United States, United Kingdom, France, Canada, Sweden, Finland, Euratom, Japan, South Korea and the Philippines.  AUSTRALIAN AID.  Concentrated in South East Asia and the South Pacific Australia's aid program contributes directly to the peace, stability and prosperity of our region.  Australia will provide some $A727.2 million in development assistance in 1982/83.  The Government accepts that Australia has a special responsibility to respond to the needs of the people and governments of the South Pacific. A new aid program to the South Pacific of $A300 million over 5 years (excluding aid to Papua New Guinea) has been introduced.  A significant feature of Australia's aid to ASEAN countries is the expansion of regional technical and economic cooperation programs.  Many Australian companies, and private consultants from a wide range of professions work with the aid program. Other initiatives taken to provide greater opportunities for Australian business participation in the aid program include:  - introduction of Australian content preference in aid purchases.  - extension of Development Import Finance Facility to all aid recipients except PNG.  - co-financing with the World Bank, using Australian goods and services.  Last year 90 per cent of Australian Bilateral Aid was spent on Australian goods and services.  $A24 million has been provided in humanitarian assistance to Cambodia and tax deductibility extended to donations to non-government overseas aid organizations.  An agricultural research center (ACIAR) has also been established in Australia to meet the needs of the developing countries.  REGIONAL INTERESTS.  Australia's close links with the Western Alliance have not adversely affected the strengthening of our ties with the developing countries of our region and the third world generally.  Australia's independent but close links with the United States and other developed countries have been viewed positively by the third world, enabling us to play a useful bridging role between the third world and the developed countries.  South East Asia and the South Pacific continue to be regions of central importance to Australia:  - Vital trade and communication lines traverse the region.  - Both are areas of strategic importance to us.  - Their security situation directly affects us.  - Australia's economic interests(particularly in ASEAN) are substantial and growing.  Australia is an important member of the South Pacific Forum and annually attends the post-ASEAN foreign Ministers' meeting.  The Commonwealth, embracing about a quarter of the world's population, remains an important and constructive force for affecting relations between developed and developing countries.  - Australia, working through the Commonwealth made a major contribution to the constitutional settlement in Zimbabwe.  - Australia hosted CHOGM in 1981 in Melbourne.  - An Australian proposal led to the holding of Commonwealth Heads of Government Regional Meetings (Sydney 1978, New Delhi 1980, Fiji 1982).  A comprehensive balanced view of the role Australia can play in the world is essential. The Government has had to work hard to earn Australia's high international reputation as a responsible and respected voice. But this reputation can so easily be undermined.  Australia's ability to defend its interests and influence events in our favor depends critically on our demonstrated capacity to honor our word and basic commitments.  DEFENSE  The Government is committed to ensure the security of Australia through a well-equipped and adequately trained Australian Defense. Force (ADF) maintaining close cooperation within our region and with our more distant allies to foster peace and stability. The 1982/83 Budget provides $4622 million for defense - about 2.9% of GDP. Up from 2.6% in 1975/76 with a target of 3% by 1984/85. Outlays on capital equipment in 1982/83 are estimated at about $690 million, an  increase of 40% on 1981/82. Obligations in later years are estimated at $4011 million.  In the current 5 year Defense Plan the permanent force will reach 76600. In June 1982 it numbered 73185, up from 71531 in June 1980. Reserve Force strength stood at 34000 in June 1982.  In 1982 new patrol boat bases were opened at Cairns and Darwin. A site for an additional base is under examination near Port Hedland. A new naval base is being completed at Cockburn Sound while in NSW the modernization of Garden Island is well under way.  A major new Army complex is now operating at Bonegilla, Victoria and new task force bases are under development at Enoggera, Townsville and Holsworthy.  In Northern Australia a highly specialized unit called NORFORCE has been established to increase surveillance in remote areas.  Learmonth Airbase has been upgraded and construction has begun on a new airbase at Derby in WA. Work has been completed to enable the redeployment of a Mirage Squadron to Darwin in mid 1983. Planning has also commenced to upgrade Tindal, NT as a major base for the new tactical fighter force.  $106 million is to be spent on new facilities at Williamtown, NSW as the major F/A 18 base.  Major equipment items introduced into service since 1976 include:  - Two Oberon class conventional submarines.  - 103 Leopard tanks.  - 2300 light trucks.  - 10 P3C Orion long-range maritime patrol aircraft.  - 12 C130H Hercules transport aircraft.  - Rapier low level air defense system.  - Amphibious Heavy Lift ship (HMAS Tobruk).  - Two guided-missile frigates (PFGs).  - Oceanographic ship.  - A reconnaissance capability for F111C aircraft and for F111A aircraft to cover attrition losses.  - Advanced technology weaponry including Mk48 submarine launched torpedoes and Harpoon anti-ship missiles.  - Six Fremantle class patrol boats.  RAN - A RECORD PEACETIME PROGRAM IS UNDERWAY.  - Contracts have been signed with Carrington Shipyard near Newcastle for the construction of two prototype inshore mine hunter catamarans.  - Williamstown Naval Dockyard in Victoria is to submit a proposal for the construction of new frigates.  - Guided Missile Frigates (FFGs)- HMAS Sydney was commissioned in January and HMAS Darwin will be delivered in March 1984, to join the HMAS Adelaide (1980) and HMAS Canberra (1981).  - Eight Fremantle Class patrol boats are under construction in Cairns shipyards.  - Modernization is underway on Destroyer Escorts HMAS Stuart and HMAS Derwent.  - A Fleet Underway Replenishment Ship, HMAS Success, is being built at Vickers Cockatoo Dockyard.  - Evaluation is underway on proposals for local construction of replacements for the River Class destroyer escorts.  - Additional Phalanx weapons systems have been ordered to provide fully automatic close-in defense against sea-skimming missiles of the Exocet type.  INCREASED MOBILITY AND FIREPOWER FOR THE ARMY.  - Manufacturing capability is being developed to produce heavy caliber ammunition and 105 mm light guns.  - 155 mm howitzers, gun tractors and ammunition vehicles are being procured in 1983/84.  - Project Raven - field communications equipment for the Army is being developed in Australia.  - First deliveries are being made of 1295 four ton and 940 eight ton trucks.  NEW CAPABILITIES AND TECHNOLOGIES FOR THE RAAF.  - The first of the new F/A-18 Hornet fighters to be in service in 1985.  - A further 10 P3C long-range maritime patrol aircraft are on order.  - F111C Radar Homing and Warning System is being upgraded.  - A contract has been let with the Australian Aircraft Consortium to design and develop a replacement pilot training aircraft.  - A contract has been awarded for a replacement helicopter trainer and light utility aircraft.  - The first Harpoon missiles have been delivered as part of the program for precision guided munitions for the Strike Force.  - Arrangements progressing for a follow-up production contract for the Barra Sonobuoy.  - Precision Approach Radar’s being installed in six major RAAF bases.  ANZUS remains vital to Australia's security and a key element in our cooperative effort. It is continually being reviewed and strengthened. Recent developments include the deployment of US B52s through Darwin, the offer of base porting facilities in WA, frequent visits by ships of the US Navy, and joint exercises.  Co-operation has been improved with the nations of South East Asia and the South West Pacific. Levels of training, consultations and project assistance are being increased with our regional neighbors under the Defense Cooperation Program totaling $43 million 1982/83.  INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT  The Department of Defense Support was established last year to maximize private sector involvement in meeting the design, development and production needs of the Australian Defense Force.  The Government has decided to expand its effort in this field:  - Private sector production and research for defense purposes will be further encouraged.  - We will examine the use of spare capacity in Defense establishments to carry out contract work where possible for the private sector.  - To build up shelf stock for export and domestic consumption, the Government will spend $8 million in addition to the present Defense vote on the manufacture of a range of items of greatest expected demand.  - Access will be provided to EFIC to cover sales of defense equipment abroad so as to enhance the prospects for defense sales in our region.
